body:
You have a PDF, and you need people to fill it out without printing, scanning, or emailing it back.

This guide covers the three ways to do that in 2026: an AI route that auto-detects fields in under a minute, the Adobe Acrobat route most teams default to, and the free online tools that work for one-off jobs.

You also get a side-by-side comparison so you pick the right tool for your file, not the one with the loudest ad. The end output can be either a web form (shareable link, responses in a dashboard) or a real fillable PDF (downloadable, signable, printable).

The right pick depends on whether the form lives online or has to keep its original PDF format. We cover both.

Quick answer

Three ways to convert any PDF into a fillable form in 2026: the AI route (Formester auto-detects fields in 20-40 seconds, free up to 100MB), the Adobe Acrobat route ($19.99/month, best for offline or DRM-locked PDFs), and free online tools like Sejda, PDF24, iLovePDF, and PDFgear (good for one-off jobs, manual field drawing).

Pick the AI route if you need a shareable link plus a response dashboard, Acrobat if the output must stay a static PDF, and a free tool if it is one file, one time.

  • Want a web form and a dashboard: Formester or Jotform are the only two that ship both routes in one product.
  • Want a fillable PDF, period: Acrobat for offline, Sejda or Smallpdf for browser.

The 3 methods, step by step

The AI route is fastest. Acrobat is for desktop-only or DRM-locked PDFs. Free online tools work for a one-off file.

Method 1

Convert with AI (Formester, free)

  1. 1

    Create a new form

    Open Formester and sign in. From the dashboard, click Create New Form, then pick Convert PDF to Formester Form. This route handles both clean digital PDFs and scanned documents, so a phone photo of a paper form works the same way as an exported invoice.

  2. 2

    Upload the PDF

    Drag the PDF into the upload zone. The AI reads the page, finds every blank line, checkbox, signature space, and label, and maps them to form fields. A typical 2-page intake form processes in 20-40 seconds. Files up to 100MB on the free plan, 1GB on Personal, 50GB on Business. Word docs work the same way.

  3. 3

    Review and edit detected fields

    The detected fields appear over the PDF preview. Click any field to change its type (text, number, email, date, dropdown, signature, file upload), rename its label, mark it required, or set conditional logic.

    Drag new fields from the side panel if the AI missed one, which usually happens on hand-drawn boxes in scanned forms.

  4. 4

    Design the form

    Open the Design tab. Drop in your logo, set primary and accent colors, pick a font, choose a layout (one question per page or all on one page). The branding kit saves once and applies to every future form. The free plan keeps Formester branding in the footer; paid plans remove it.

  5. 5

    Publish and share

    Click Publish. You get a shareable link, an embed snippet for any site (WordPress, Webflow, Wix, raw HTML), a QR code for printed materials, and an email-embed code that drops the first question into the body of an email.

    Submissions land in your dashboard; route them to Slack, Google Sheets, HubSpot, or Zapier without code.

  6. 6

    Optional: export filled PDFs

    If the output needs to stay a PDF (legal forms, certificates, signed contracts, government submissions), turn on the PDF Editor in form settings. Re-upload the original PDF as the template. Drag each web-form field onto the matching spot.

    Every submission then produces a filled, downloadable PDF, auto-sent to the respondent's email if you want. The dashboard still captures the structured data, so you get both formats from one submission.

Method 2

Convert with Adobe Acrobat ($19.99/month)

  1. 1

    Open in Acrobat Pro

    Open the PDF in Adobe Acrobat Pro. The conversion happens inside Acrobat in five clicks.

  2. 2

    Run Prepare Form

    Tools, Prepare Form. Acrobat scans the page and proposes form fields. On scanned documents, Acrobat runs OCR first; scan-to-form quality varies, so check every detected field.

  3. 3

    Edit field properties

    Set field types, required flags, and labels. Rename anything Acrobat got wrong.

  4. 4

    Save and distribute

    File, Save As. Distribute by email or save to a network share.

  5. 5

    Optional: enable Reader Extensions

    Turn on Reader Extensions so anyone with free Acrobat Reader can fill and save the file. Skip this and respondents need Acrobat Pro to save their progress.

Method 3

Free online tools (one-off jobs)

  1. 1

    Pick a tool

    Sejda PDF Forms (3 tasks per hour, 50MB or 200 pages free), PDF24 Tools (free, ad-supported), iLovePDF PDF Forms (auto-detects if the source PDF already has fields), or PDFgear (free, no daily cap).

  2. 2

    Upload and draw fields

    Upload the PDF, then draw form fields manually over each blank area. None of the free tools auto-detect fields on scanned documents the way the AI route does.

  3. 3

    Download the fillable PDF

    Save the fillable PDF locally and email it to respondents. Output is a PDF only, no shareable web form, no response dashboard, no native CRM routing. Skip these tools when you process more than ten of these a month, because drawing fields by hand on file number eleven costs more than any paid plan.

Frequently asked questions

Common questions about converting any PDF, scanned or digital, into a fillable form.

Is there a free way to convert a PDF to a fillable form?
Yes. Formester's free plan covers the full AI conversion flow (upload, auto-detect, publish) with files up to 100MB. PDF24, PDFgear, and the Sejda free tier (3 tasks per hour) also work for one-off jobs. Adobe Acrobat is paid only.
Can I convert a scanned paper PDF, not just a digital one?
Yes. Formester, Adobe Acrobat, Sejda, Smallpdf, iLovePDF, PDF24, and PDFgear all run OCR on scanned PDFs. Only Formester and Acrobat auto-detect fields after OCR; the rest expect you to draw fields manually.
Does the converted form keep the original PDF format?
Two answers depending on the route. The AI route publishes a web form; the original PDF is the template, the output is a shareable link. The PDF Editor route (or the Adobe Acrobat route) preserves the PDF format: every submission produces a filled, downloadable PDF that looks identical to the original.
How do I add e-signatures?
Drop a signature field anywhere on the form. Respondents sign with a finger on mobile, a mouse on desktop, or by typing their name in a script font. The signature is captured with timestamp and IP for audit. Available on the Formester signature feature.
Can I send the filled PDF back to the respondent automatically?
Yes on Formester (turn on auto-send in form settings; Business plan and above for the auto-PDF feature). Adobe Acrobat with Acrobat Sign also does this. Free online tools generally do not. You can also export submissions as PDF in bulk from the dashboard.
What file size can I upload?
Formester: 100MB free, 1GB Personal, 50GB Business per file. Sejda free: 50MB or 200 pages. Smallpdf free: ~5MB. Acrobat Pro: practically unlimited (limited by your machine).
Is the conversion accessible (WCAG / 508)?
Web forms are easier to make accessible than PDFs. Formester's web output supports keyboard navigation, screen readers, and color-contrast settings out of the box. For Acrobat's PDF route, you need to set the Tags tree manually after conversion, which is the most common gap in agency workflows.
Can I connect submissions to Google Sheets, Slack, or my CRM?
Yes on Formester and Jotform via native integrations. On the PDF-only tools (Sejda, PDF24, Smallpdf), you get an emailed PDF; routing to a CRM requires Zapier or manual upload.
Does the AI detect every field, every time?
No tool does. Clean digital PDFs hit close to 95-100% on basic fields. Scanned phone photos with shadows or skew drop to 70-85%. The fix is always the same: review the detected fields once, fix any miss, save the template, and the next 100 conversions of the same form are perfect.
Can I make a fillable PDF from a Word document?
Yes. Export the Word doc as a PDF first (File, Save As, PDF), then run it through any of the three methods in this guide. Formester also accepts the Word file directly.
